vulnerabilities.description: Authentication token fetched but not transmitted to API. Token is retrieved via getAccessTokenSilently() but never added to request headers, defeating auth mechanism
vulnerabilities.code_snippet:
const token = await getAccessTokenSilently();
// ... token never used in fetch headers
vulnerabilities.impact: API endpoints may not be authenticating requests, allowing unauthorized access if backend relies on header-based auth
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add Authorization header: headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`; OR verify backend uses cookie-based session validation

vulnerabilities.description: File upload endpoint called without Authorization header despite fetching token. FormData is sent without auth credentials
vulnerabilities.impact: Evidence upload endpoint may not authenticate user, allowing unauthorized file uploads
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Include token in query parameter or Authorization header for multipart/form-data requests

vulnerabilities.description: File type validation relies only on client-side MIME type checking. File.type property can be spoofed
vulnerabilities.impact: Attacker can bypass client validation by spoofing MIME type, uploading malicious files (executables, scripts)
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement server-side magic byte validation. CLAUDE.md mentions this exists, but ensure it's enforced on all file uploads

vulnerabilities.description: User-provided facts and names interpolated directly into AI prompt without sanitization
vulnerabilities.impact: Prompt injection attack: user can craft facts/names to manipulate AI behavior, bypass instructions, extract system prompts
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Sanitize user input before including in prompts. Use structured prompting with separated user input fields

vulnerabilities.description: User input (names, document title) assigned directly to state without client-side validation before sending to API
vulnerabilities.impact: While CLAUDE.md indicates server-side Zod validation exists, client should validate length, special characters early
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add client-side validation: max length, character whitelist, required field checks

vulnerabilities.description: File upload logging includes documentId and evidence details without access control verification
vulnerabilities.code_snippet:
console.log('🔼 Upload initiated:', {
  hasFile: !!selectedFile,
  hasEvidence: !!evidence,
  hasDocId: !!documentId,
  evidenceId: evidence?.id
vulnerabilities.impact: Browser console logs may be captured by malicious scripts or visible to other users on shared devices
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove sensitive data from logs, or only log in development mode

vulnerabilities.description: Error details displayed in DOM (development only). While React escapes content, best practice is to avoid raw error output
vulnerabilities.impact: Low risk due to development-only guard and React escaping, but error stacks could leak implementation details
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Limit error details to non-sensitive information; implement error tracking service (Sentry) instead

vulnerabilities.description: TOS acceptance flag stored in localStorage without encryption. While authenticated, key is predictable (tos_accepted_${user.sub})
vulnerabilities.impact: User sub is visible; localStorage is domain-accessible by any script on domain; attacker could set flag to bypass TOS
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use sessionStorage instead (cleared on logout), rely on server-side TOS verification as source of truth

vulnerabilities.description: Multiple concurrent save operations possible if user rapidly clicks save button or auto-save triggers
vulnerabilities.code_snippet:
const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false);
// In handleSave, if isSaving is false, can start new save while previous completes
vulnerabilities.impact: Low risk due to idempotent nature of save operations, but could cause inconsistent UI state
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Ensure save handler properly guards against concurrent calls using isSaving state flag

vulnerabilities.description: AffidavitForm.js imports from 'lodash' - large library, consider tree-shaking
vulnerabilities.impact: Entire lodash library bundled even if only debounce used. Low security risk but bloats bundle
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use lodash.debounce or implement lightweight debounce: const debounce = (fn, delay) => { let timer; return (...args) => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => fn(...args), delay); }; }

vulnerabilities.description: UserDashboard.js correctly uses useAuthenticatedApi() helper, but other components fetch tokens manually and don't use them
vulnerabilities.impact: Inconsistent auth patterns suggest copy-paste errors or misunderstanding of auth model
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Audit all API calls. Replace manual token patterns with useAuthenticatedApi() helper consistently

strengths: Input validation with Zod on Route Handlers
Proper React escaping prevents DOM-based XSS
No hardcoded API secrets in client code
Stripe webhook signature verification uses raw body
critical_issues: Multiple API endpoints called without Auth header despite fetching token (5 instances) - suggests either missing security or auth tokens improperly configured
Client-side file type validation can be easily bypassed - no magic byte checking on client
Prompt injection risk via unsanitized user input in AI prompts
summary.root_cause_analysis: The codebase appears to rely on cookie-based auth (per CLAUDE.md: '@auth0/nextjs-auth0 v3, cookie session'). However, fetching tokens and not using them suggests either: (1) developer confusion about the auth model, (2) incomplete refactoring from bearer token to cookie-based auth, or (3) cargo-cult code copying. The useAuthenticatedApi() helper exists but isn't used consistently.

recommendations.action: Audit and fix all API authentication calls. Either: (a) add Authorization headers to all token-fetching components, OR (b) remove all getAccessTokenSilently() calls if relying on cookies. Verify with backend engineer which auth model is intended.
Verify server-side file upload validation with magic byte checking. Document that client-side MIME validation can be spoofed and must never be sole validation method.
Replace all manual token handling with consistent useAuthenticatedApi() helper. Enforce pattern via ESLint rule.
recommendations.implementation: Create ESLint rule to catch 'getAccessTokenSilently' outside of proper auth context

recommendations.action: Implement prompt injection protection. Sanitize user inputs before including in AI prompts. Use structured fields instead of interpolation.
Remove or redact sensitive data from console.log statements. Implement structured logging via error tracking service.
Add client-side input validation for all user inputs with max lengths, character restrictions, required field checks.
Use sessionStorage instead of localStorage for TOS flag; rely on server-side verification as source of truth.
Replace lodash.debounce with lightweight custom implementation or use lodash.debounce only.

testing_recommendations: Penetration test: Attempt to call API endpoints with missing/invalid tokens
Security test: Spoof file MIME types in evidence upload and verify server rejects
Prompt injection test: Inject prompt-breaking characters in fact inputs and verify output
Auth flow test: Verify token is present in all authenticated API requests via browser DevTools Network tab
XSS test: Attempt to inject HTML/scripts in name, fact, and document title fields
